questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with regular 28-day menstrual cycles comes to the clinic for preconception counseling. She asks how many days before ovulation intercourse can still result in pregnancy. Based on the survival of gametes in the female reproductive tract, which of the following is the most accurate answer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1 day

choices.label: B
choices.text: 2 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: 5 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: 7 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: 10 days

explanation.summary: Sperm survive 3 to 5 days in the female reproductive tract, so intercourse up to 5 days before ovulation can produce a pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fertilization must occur within about 24 hours of ovulation, but sperm can live for three to five days in the reproductive tract. Pregnancy is therefore possible from intercourse up to five days before ovulation, although the chance is highest within 24 hours of ovulation and the day before.

whyWrongByChoice.A: One day describes the window during which the ovulated egg remains fertilizable, not the limit of sperm survival before ovulation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Two days is within the fertile window but understates it; sperm survival extends the window to about five days.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Seven days exceeds the maximum sperm survival of three to five days in the reproductive tract.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ten days far exceeds sperm survival; conception from intercourse this early is not possible.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman undergoing fertility treatment has an oocyte retrieved from the fallopian tube shortly after ovulation, before any exposure to sperm. Examination of the cell's nuclear contents would show it arrested at which of the following stages?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anaphase of meiosis I

choices.label: B
choices.text: Metaphase of meiosis I

choices.label: C
choices.text: Metaphase of meiosis II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prophase of meiosis I

choices.label: E
choices.text: Telophase of meiosis II

explanation.summary: The ovulated secondary oocyte is arrested at metaphase of meiosis II and completes meiosis II only if fertilization occurs.
explanation.whyCorrect: The LH surge drives the primary oocyte to complete meiosis I, producing a secondary oocyte and the first polar body. The secondary oocyte enters meiosis II but arrests at metaphase II, and it remains there at ovulation until sperm penetration triggers completion of meiosis II with extrusion of the second polar body.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anaphase I occurs during completion of meiosis I prior to ovulation; the released cell has already finished this division.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Meiosis I is completed under the influence of the LH surge before ovulation, so the released cell has passed metaphase I.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prophase I is where the primary oocyte is arrested from fetal life until the LH surge at puberty, before ovulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Telophase II occurs only after fertilization triggers completion of meiosis II; an unfertilized oocyte never reaches it.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman gives birth to an infant with hypotonia and characteristic facial features. Karyotype of the infant shows 47,XX,+21, and studies indicate the extra chromosome is maternal in origin. Which of the following age-related changes in the mother's oocytes most likely predisposed to this outcome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accumulated replication errors from repeated mitoses

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decline in chromatid cohesion and spindle integrity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failure of crossing over during prophase I

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of cortical granules from the oocyte cortex

choices.label: E
choices.text: Premature completion of meiosis II before ovulation

explanation.summary: Prolonged meiotic arrest in aging oocytes degrades cohesion and spindle integrity, predisposing to nondisjunction and trisomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Female meiosis begins in fetal life and remains arrested for decades. With increasing maternal age, cohesion between chromatids and spindle integrity decline, predisposing to nondisjunction, most commonly during meiosis I but also during meiosis II. Fertilization of the resulting egg carrying an extra chromosome 21 by a normal haploid sperm produces trisomy 21.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cumulative replication errors from ongoing mitotic divisions describe the paternal-age effect in spermatogenesis, producing de novo mutations rather than maternal trisomy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Crossing over in prophase I generates genetic diversity; its failure is not the described mechanism of age-related aneuploidy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cortical granules prevent polyspermy after fertilization; their loss would not cause a maternally derived extra chromosome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Meiosis II in the oocyte completes only after fertilization; it does not finish prematurely before ovulation.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man and his 30-year-old partner have a child diagnosed with an autosomal dominant disorder caused by a de novo point mutation shown to be of paternal origin. Which of the following features of spermatogenesis best explains the association between advanced paternal age and this type of mutation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Exposure of sperm to the acidic environment of the vagina

choices.label: B
choices.text: Incomplete capacitation of sperm in the female reproductive tract

choices.label: C
choices.text: Numerous mitotic divisions of spermatogonia with repeated DNA replication

choices.label: D
choices.text: Progressive loss of cohesion between sister chromatids with age

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prolonged meiotic arrest of primary spermatocytes over decades

explanation.summary: Continuous spermatogonial mitoses throughout adult life accumulate DNA replication errors, making sperm a major source of de novo mutations with advancing paternal age.
explanation.whyCorrect: Spermatogenesis involves continuous cell division throughout adult life, with spermatogonia undergoing numerous mitotic divisions before entering meiosis. Each round of DNA replication carries a risk of error, so the mutation burden rises with paternal age, making spermatogenesis a significant source of de novo mutations.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Vaginal acidity kills sperm outright; it is a barrier to fertilization, not a cause of heritable point mutations.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Capacitation affects a sperm's ability to fertilize the egg; it does not alter the DNA sequence carried by the sperm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Age-related decline in cohesion and spindle integrity is the maternal mechanism predisposing to aneuploidy, not point mutations of paternal origin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prolonged meiotic arrest is a feature of oogenesis, not spermatogenesis; spermatocytes begin meiosis at puberty and complete it in the testes without decades-long arrest.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman presents with 6 weeks of amenorrhea and new right lower quadrant pain. A serum human chorionic gonadotropin test is positive, and transvaginal ultrasound shows no intrauterine pregnancy but reveals a right adnexal mass. The abnormally implanted tissue is most likely located in which of the following sites?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ampulla of the fallopian tube

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cervical canal of the uterus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Graafian follicle of the ovary

choices.label: D
choices.text: Interstitial uterotubal junction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peritoneal cavity of the pelvis

explanation.summary: Ectopic pregnancy most often implants in the fallopian tube, specifically the ampulla, the usual site of fertilization.
explanation.whyCorrect: The egg normally meets the sperm in the ampulla, in the distal third of the fallopian tube. When the fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, the most common location is the fallopian tube, specifically the ampulla. Diagnosis uses an hCG blood test to confirm pregnancy and ultrasound to determine location, and the ectopic tissue must be removed medically or surgically because tubal rupture and bleeding are life-threatening.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cervical implantation is not the typical location; the cervix acts mainly as a barrier to ascending sperm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ovary releases the oocyte but is not the most common site of ectopic implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The uterotubal junction is a selective barrier for sperm transit, not the most common ectopic site.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Abdominal (peritoneal) implantation occurs but is far less common than implantation in the ampulla.

questions.stem: In an assisted reproduction laboratory, freshly ejaculated sperm placed directly with mature oocytes fail to fertilize them, whereas sperm first incubated in medium that mimics female reproductive tract secretions succeed. The change induced by this incubation is best characterized by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Exocytosis of cortical granules at the oocyte cell membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: Extrusion of the second polar body from the maturing oocyte

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fusion of the sperm membrane with the oocyte plasma membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of sperm surface antigens with activation of tail motility

choices.label: E
choices.text: Release of hydrolytic enzymes from the acrosomal cap at the zona

explanation.summary: Capacitation is a biochemical change during transit that strips surface antigens, activates the tail, and primes the acrosome via rising calcium and cAMP.
explanation.whyCorrect: During transit through the female tract, in part through interaction with cervical secretions, sperm undergo capacitation. They lose surface antigens, which facilitates binding to the egg, and their motility increases through tail activation. A gradual increase in intracellular calcium enhances cAMP generation, priming the sperm for the acrosome reaction; only capacitated sperm can fertilize an ovum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cortical granule exocytosis is the ovum's response to fertilization that prevents polyspermy, not a change in sperm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Polar body extrusion is a feature of oocyte meiosis, not of sperm maturation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Membrane fusion occurs at the oolemma after the sperm has penetrated the egg's outer layers, downstream of capacitation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Acrosomal enzyme release is the acrosome reaction, a later event at the zona pellucida for which capacitation merely primes the sperm.

questions.stem: During fertilization, hundreds of capacitated sperm bind to receptors in the zona pellucida of an ovulated oocyte. Which of the following events most directly enables a bound sperm to traverse this glycoprotein layer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Binding of sperm fertilin to integrin on the oocyte membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: Buffering of the local environment by alkaline semen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ciliary currents generated by the fallopian tube epithelium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exocytosis of lysosomal enzymes from cortical granules

choices.label: E
choices.text: Release of acrosin and other hydrolytic enzymes from the sperm head

explanation.summary: The acrosome reaction releases hydrolytic enzymes such as acrosin that, with sperm motility, allow penetration of the zona pellucida.
explanation.whyCorrect: After binding to zona pellucida receptors, a calcium surge within the sperm triggers the acrosome reaction. The released hydrolytic enzymes, including acrosin, degrade the egg's layers and, together with exposed sperm-surface proteins and sperm motility, create a tunnel through which the head, neck, and middle piece enter the egg.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fertilin-integrin binding mediates fusion at the oocyte plasma membrane after the zona has already been crossed.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Alkaline semen buffers vaginal acidity early in transit; it plays no role at the zona pellucida.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ciliary movement propels the ovum and later the zygote along the tube; it does not carry sperm through the zona.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cortical granule exocytosis comes from the ovum after fertilization and blocks additional sperm; it does not help sperm penetrate.

questions.stem: A fertilization study examines a zygote that arrested early in development and is found to contain one maternal and two paternal chromosome complements along with an abnormal centrosome number. Failure of which of the following processes most likely allowed this abnormality to occur?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Calcium-triggered exocytosis of cortical granules by the ovum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Calcium-triggered release of acrosomal enzymes by the sperm

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capacitation of sperm during transit through the tract

choices.label: D
choices.text: Completion of meiosis II by the fertilized oocyte

choices.label: E
choices.text: Segregation of sister chromatids during meiosis II

explanation.summary: The cortical reaction, triggered by a rise in intracellular calcium in the ovum, blocks polyspermy; its failure permits a second sperm to enter.
explanation.whyCorrect: Two paternal chromosome sets with an abnormal centrosome complement indicate polyspermy, which usually prevents viable zygote development. Normally, fertilization by one sperm raises intracellular calcium in the ovum and triggers the cortical reaction: cortical granules release lysosomal enzymes that make the plasma membrane impenetrable and alter the zona pellucida so no additional sperm can bind.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The acrosome reaction enables the first sperm to penetrate; its failure would prevent fertilization, not cause dispermy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Failed capacitation would leave sperm unable to fertilize at all, producing no zygote rather than a dispermic one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Failure to complete meiosis II would alter the maternal contribution, not add an extra paternal chromosome set.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A meiosis II segregation error causes trisomy of a single chromosome, not an entire extra paternal genome with extra centrosomes.

questions.stem: Shortly after ovulation, a released oocyte is captured by the fimbriae of the fallopian tube. The outermost cellular layer surrounding the oocyte contributes most directly to this capture through which of the following properties?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adhesion molecules on retained granulosa cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cilia that beat toward the uterine cavity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycoprotein receptors that bind capacitated sperm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Integrin receptors on the plasma membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lysosomal enzymes stored in cortical granules

explanation.summary: The corona radiata consists of granulosa cells rich in adhesion molecules that help the fimbriae capture the ovum.
explanation.whyCorrect: The corona radiata is made of follicular (granulosa) cells that formed around the developing oocyte and remain attached when the egg is released. These cells are rich in adhesion molecules that help the ovum be captured by the fimbriae of the fallopian tube, and the corona is also the first layer sperm must penetrate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cilia belong to the fallopian tube lining, not to the cell layers of the ovum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sperm-binding glycoprotein receptors belong to the zona pellucida, the layer deep to the corona radiata, and serve fertilization rather than capture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Integrin is the receptor on the oocyte plasma membrane that binds sperm fertilin; it does not mediate fimbrial capture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cortical granules lie beneath the oocyte plasma membrane and act after fertilization to prevent polyspermy.

questions.stem: During in vitro studies of fertilization, a sperm that has passed through the corona radiata and zona pellucida reaches the outer surface of the egg itself. Interaction between which of the following pairs of molecules most directly mediates binding and fusion of the two cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acrosin on the sperm and glycoproteins of the zona pellucida

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adhesion molecules on granulosa cells and receptors on the fimbriae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cortical granule enzymes and receptors on the sperm midpiece

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fertilin on the sperm head and integrin on the oocyte membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surface antigens on the sperm and phagocyte receptors in the uterus

explanation.summary: Fertilin on the sperm head binds integrin on the oocyte plasma membrane to mediate sperm-egg binding and membrane fusion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sperm and ovum bind with the help of surface proteins on both cells: fertilin is a protein on the head of the spermatozoon, and integrin is its receptor on the oocyte plasma membrane. Both facilitate binding and fusion of the plasma membranes, after which the sperm's head, neck, and middle piece enter the egg and release its genetic material.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acrosin is a hydrolytic acrosomal enzyme that degrades the zona pellucida; it acts before the sperm reaches the plasma membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Adhesion molecules of the corona radiata help the fimbriae capture the ovum, not bind sperm to the oolemma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cortical granule enzymes act after fertilization to make the membrane impenetrable; they do not mediate sperm binding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uterine phagocytes destroy sperm during transit; this interaction eliminates sperm rather than mediating fusion.

questions.stem: A cell biologist analyzes the gamete released from a woman's ovary at ovulation, before any contact with sperm. Which of the following best describes the chromosome number and DNA content of this cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 23 chromosomes, 1C DNA content

choices.label: B
choices.text: 23 chromosomes, 2C DNA content

choices.label: C
choices.text: 46 chromosomes, 2C DNA content

choices.label: D
choices.text: 46 chromosomes, 4C DNA content

choices.label: E
choices.text: 92 chromosomes, 4C DNA content

explanation.summary: The ovulated secondary oocyte is haploid with duplicated chromatids: 23 chromosomes (1N) and 2C DNA content.
explanation.whyCorrect: The LH surge drives completion of meiosis I, which separates homologous chromosomes and produces a secondary oocyte (1N, 2C) plus the first polar body. This secondary oocyte arrests at metaphase II and is the cell released at ovulation; it reaches 1N, 1C only after fertilization triggers completion of meiosis II.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 23 chromosomes with 1C content describes the mature ovum, which forms only after fertilization completes meiosis II.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 46 chromosomes with 2C content describes a diploid cell such as an oogonium before DNA replication, not the ovulated gamete.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 46 chromosomes with 4C content describes the primary oocyte after S phase, arrested in meiosis I before the LH surge.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 92 chromosomes never occur in normal gametogenesis; DNA replication doubles content to 4C without doubling the chromosome count to 92.

questions.stem: Of the millions of sperm deposited in the female reproductive tract during intercourse, only a tiny number reach the site of fertilization. The largest proportion of sperm is destroyed shortly after ejaculation by which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acidity of the vaginal environment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enzymes released during the cortical reaction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hydrolytic enzymes within the zona pellucida

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mechanical obstruction at the uterotubal junction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Phagocytes residing in the uterine cavity

explanation.summary: The acidic vaginal environment kills the majority of sperm shortly after ejaculation, forming the first major barrier to fertilization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Many of the millions of sperm entering the vagina are rapidly destroyed by its acidic environment, and only a small fraction passes through the cervix. Alkaline components of semen and cervical mucus buffer the acid, providing temporary protection so some sperm can transit into the uterus.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The cortical reaction occurs in the ovum after fertilization to block polyspermy; it does not destroy sperm in transit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The zona pellucida selects and binds sperm at the egg itself; it is not responsible for the massive early loss of sperm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The uterotubal junction is a major selective barrier, but it acts on the small population that survives the vagina, cervix, and uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uterine phagocytes destroy sperm later in transit, after most have already been killed in the vagina.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is undergoing an evaluation of ovarian steroid synthesis. In the outer cells of her ovarian follicles, luteinizing hormone binds its receptor and initiates steroidogenesis from cholesterol that has diffused in from neighboring blood vessels. Which of the following enzymes catalyzes the first step of this pathway in these cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase

choices.label: B
choices.text: 21-hydroxylase

choices.label: C
choices.text: 5-alpha-reductase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aromatase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Desmolase

explanation.summary: In theca cells, desmolase converts cholesterol to pregnenolone, the first step toward androstenedione.
explanation.whyCorrect: Theca cells form the outer layer of the follicle and contact blood vessels, allowing cholesterol to diffuse in. After LH binds its theca-cell receptor, desmolase converts cholesterol to pregnenolone; several steps later the pathway yields androstenedione.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase interconverts estrone and estradiol; it does not act on cholesterol.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 21-hydroxylase functions in adrenal corticosteroid pathways, not in the LH-stimulated theca-cell step described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 5-alpha-reductase converts testosterone to a more potent androgen and is not the cholesterol-to-pregnenolone step.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aromatase acts in granulosa cells, converting androstenedione to 17beta-estradiol under FSH stimulation, not in theca cells on cholesterol.

questions.stem: Radiolabeled androstenedione is tracked within a developing ovarian follicle. It diffuses out of the cell that produced it and is converted to 17beta-estradiol in a neighboring cell. Which of the following is the cell in which this conversion occurs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anterior pituitary gonadotroph

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endometrial gland cell

choices.label: C
choices.text: Granulosa cell

choices.label: D
choices.text: Secondary oocyte

choices.label: E
choices.text: Theca cell

explanation.summary: Granulosa cells contain aromatase, which converts theca-derived androstenedione to 17beta-estradiol.
explanation.whyCorrect: Androstenedione made in theca cells diffuses to the more interiorly located granulosa cells. When FSH binds its granulosa-cell receptor, aromatase is induced and converts androstenedione to 17beta-estradiol.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gonadotrophs release LH and FSH; they do not convert androgens to estrogens.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endometrial gland cells are hormone targets, not sites of ovarian estradiol synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The oocyte is surrounded by granulosa cells but is not the site of aromatization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The theca cell produces androstenedione but lacks the aromatase step; the androgen leaves this cell for conversion.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer is offered endocrine therapy. He asks how his body makes estrogen when he has no ovaries. Which of the following best explains his source of estrogen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conversion of androstenedione by aromatase in adipose tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of cholesterol to estradiol in a single hepatic step

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct secretion of 17beta-estradiol by the anterior pituitary

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release of stored estradiol from corticosteroid-binding globulin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Secretion of estrone by luteinized follicular cells in the testis

explanation.summary: Extragonadal aromatase in tissues such as fat, bone, skin, brain, and breast converts androgens to estrogens in males.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aromatase is expressed outside the gonads, including in adipose tissue, liver, bone, skin, brain, and breast. There it converts androstenedione to estrone and testosterone to 17beta-estradiol, which accounts for estrogen in males and is why aromatase inhibition lowers his estrogen levels.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cholesterol is the steroid precursor, but synthesis proceeds through pregnenolone and androgens over several steps, not one hepatic conversion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The anterior pituitary releases LH and FSH; it does not secrete estradiol.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Binding globulins transport steroid hormones in plasma; they are not a storage source that generates estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Luteinized follicular cells form the corpus luteum in the ovary; there is no such source in the testis.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman had her last menstrual period 6 years ago. Depletion of her ovarian follicle pool has ended cyclic ovarian activity. Which of the following is the predominant circulating estrogen in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 17beta-estradiol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Androstenedione

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pregnenolone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Progesterone

explanation.summary: After menopause, peripheral aromatization makes estrone the predominant circulating estrogen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once the ovarian follicle pool is depleted, cyclic ovarian estradiol production ceases. Peripheral aromatization of androstenedione in extragonadal tissues becomes the main estrogen source, and estrone predominates in the circulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 17beta-estradiol is the principal estrogen during reproductive years, when granulosa cells produce it cyclically.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Androstenedione is an androgen precursor of estrone, not an estrogen itself.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pregnenolone is an early steroid intermediate formed by desmolase, not a circulating estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progesterone is a progestogen, not an estrogen, and luteal production stops without ovulation.

questions.stem: In an experiment, gonadotropin-releasing hormone is administered to healthy volunteers as a continuous intravenous infusion rather than in pulses. After several days, serum LH and FSH concentrations fall. Which of the following best explains this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blockade of the hypophyseal-portal vasculature

choices.label: B
choices.text: Degeneration of the corpus luteum with loss of progesterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Downregulation of GnRH receptors in the anterior pituitary

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased inhibin secretion from granulosa cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Positive feedback by estradiol on the hypothalamus

explanation.summary: GnRH must be pulsatile; continuous exposure downregulates its pituitary receptors and lowers LH and FSH.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pulsatile release of hypothalamic GnRH is the basis for all reproductive hormone changes. If GnRH is delivered continuously, its receptors on the anterior pituitary are downregulated, decreasing LH and FSH secretion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: GnRH still reaches the pituitary in this experiment; the portal route is intact and is not the mechanism of the decline.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Corpus luteum degeneration lowers progesterone and leads to menstruation; it does not suppress gonadotropins via GnRH exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin selectively lowers FSH; it does not explain the fall in both gonadotropins caused by the infusion itself.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sustained high estradiol near the end of the follicular phase produces positive feedback and an LH surge, the opposite of the observed fall in LH.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman with regular 28-day cycles is studied across one cycle. For most of the follicular phase, rising estradiol suppresses gonadotropin secretion, yet at midcycle a surge of LH triggers ovulation. Which of the following best explains the surge?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activin from the ovary directly triggers a burst of LH release

choices.label: B
choices.text: Falling estradiol releases the pituitary from feedback inhibition

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibin from granulosa cells selectively augments LH secretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rising progesterone from the corpus luteum stimulates gonadotrophs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sustained high estradiol switches its feedback from negative to positive

explanation.summary: Near the end of the follicular phase, sustained high estradiol exerts positive feedback that produces the ovulatory LH surge.
explanation.whyCorrect: During most of the follicular phase, estradiol provides negative feedback that suppresses gonadotropin secretion. Near the end of the follicular phase, sustained high estradiol levels switch to positive feedback on the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary, producing the LH surge that triggers ovulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Activin promotes FSH synthesis and secretion; it is not described as triggering the LH surge.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Estradiol is high, not falling, just before the surge; the surge results from feedback reversal, not withdrawal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin selectively decreases FSH secretion; it does not augment LH.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The corpus luteum forms after ovulation, so its progesterone cannot cause the midcycle surge.

questions.stem: During the follicular phase, several follicles begin to develop, but normally only one dominant follicle matures and ovulates. A hormone secreted by granulosa cells reaches the anterior pituitary and selectively reduces the secretion of a single gonadotropin, starving less-responsive follicles of support. Which of the following is this hormone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibin

explanation.summary: Granulosa-cell inhibin selectively suppresses FSH, restricting continued maturation to the dominant follicle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inhibin is secreted by granulosa cells and travels to the anterior pituitary, where it selectively provides negative feedback that decreases FSH secretion. The resulting decline in FSH stops the growth of less-responsive follicles, so a single dominant follicle matures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Activin does the opposite: it promotes FSH synthesis and secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Estradiol feedback suppresses gonadotropin secretion broadly during the follicular phase rather than selectively targeting FSH from granulosa cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GnRH is the hypothalamic releasing hormone that stimulates, rather than selectively suppresses, gonadotropin secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hCG is produced by the early embryo to rescue the corpus luteum; it plays no role in follicle selection.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman has a positive pregnancy test 4 weeks after her last menstrual period. Her endometrium remains intact because the corpus luteum has continued to produce progesterone instead of degenerating. Which of the following hormones is responsible for preserving the corpus luteum?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Follicle-stimulating hormone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

explanation.summary: hCG from the early embryo prevents involution of the corpus luteum, maintaining progesterone and the endometrium.
explanation.whyCorrect: When fertilization and implantation occur, the early embryo produces human chorionic gonadotropin. hCG prevents degradation (involution) of the corpus luteum, so progesterone production continues, maintaining the endometrium and the pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: FSH induces aromatase in granulosa cells during follicular development; it does not rescue the corpus luteum in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GnRH drives pituitary LH and FSH release and is not the embryo-derived rescue signal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin selectively suppresses FSH secretion and has no role in maintaining the corpus luteum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: LH stimulates theca cells and surges at ovulation, but it is not the pregnancy signal that prevents luteal involution.

questions.stem: A researcher studies how 17beta-estradiol alters gene expression in breast tissue. After the hormone dissociates from its plasma carrier and diffuses across the plasma membrane, which of the following events allows it to regulate transcription of target genes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hormone activates a surface G protein-coupled receptor that raises cAMP

choices.label: B
choices.text: The hormone binds a receptor tyrosine kinase that phosphorylates cytosolic targets

choices.label: C
choices.text: The hormone binds ribosomes directly and accelerates translation of mRNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hormone opens a ligand-gated ion channel that depolarizes the cell

choices.label: E
choices.text: The hormone-receptor complex dimerizes and binds estrogen-response elements in DNA

explanation.summary: Estrogen binds intracellular receptors that dimerize, bind estrogen-response elements, and act as transcription factors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estrogen receptors are located primarily in the nucleus, with additional populations in the cytoplasm and at the plasma membrane. After binding, the activated receptors form a dimer that binds specific DNA sequences called estrogen-response elements, and the hormone-receptor dimer becomes a transcription factor regulating mRNA production.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estradiol is a steroid that diffuses across the membrane to intracellular receptors; its genomic action is not through cAMP-linked surface receptors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Receptor tyrosine kinase signaling is not the described mechanism for estrogen's regulation of transcription.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The hormone-receptor complex acts on DNA to regulate transcription; it does not act directly on ribosomes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Steroid hormone effects develop slowly through gene transcription, unlike rapid ion-channel signaling.

questions.stem: A physiologist measures the distribution of progesterone in the plasma of a healthy 30-year-old woman during the luteal phase. Because the hormone is lipid-soluble and does not freely dissolve in plasma, most of it is transported bound to protein. Progesterone circulates primarily bound to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Albumin and corticosteroid-binding globulin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Albumin and sex hormone-binding globulin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Corticosteroid-binding globulin and hemoglobin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Free hormone dissolved directly in plasma water

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sex hormone-binding globulin and inhibin

explanation.summary: Progesterone circulates mainly bound to albumin and corticosteroid-binding globulin, both made in the liver.
explanation.whyCorrect: Steroid hormones are lipid-soluble and do not freely dissolve in plasma. Progesterone circulates primarily bound to albumin and corticosteroid-binding globulin, whereas estrogens travel mainly on albumin and sex hormone-binding globulin; these carrier proteins are synthesized in the liver.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Albumin plus sex hormone-binding globulin is the primary carrier combination for estrogens, not progesterone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemoglobin carries oxygen within red cells and is not a progesterone transport protein.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progesterone is lipid-soluble and cannot circulate mainly as free hormone dissolved in plasma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibin is a granulosa-cell hormone that suppresses FSH; it is not a plasma steroid carrier.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman who went through menopause at age 51 sustains a vertebral compression fracture. Bone densitometry shows osteoporosis. Which of the following mechanisms best explains her bone loss?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased apoptosis and increased activity of osteoclasts

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased number of bone-resorbing osteoclasts in bone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated progesterone suppressing bone formation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excess estradiol stimulating bone resorption

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased apoptosis of bone-resorbing osteoclasts

explanation.summary: Estradiol deficiency increases osteoclast number and activity, partly by decreasing osteoclast apoptosis, causing bone resorption and osteoporosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estrogen normally increases bone mass. After menopause, loss of estradiol decreases apoptosis of osteoclasts and increases their activity, so the number and activity of bone-resorbing cells rise. The resulting increase in bone resorption substantially weakens bone and raises fracture risk.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Osteoclast numbers increase in this state; a decrease would reduce resorption rather than cause osteoporosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Postmenopausal progesterone is low, and the brick attributes bone loss to estradiol deficiency, not progesterone excess.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Her estradiol is deficient after menopause; excess estradiol is not present and estrogen supports bone mass.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estradiol loss decreases, not increases, osteoclast apoptosis, allowing these cells to persist and resorb bone.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman tracking her fertility notices that her basal body temperature rises by about half a degree shortly after ovulation and stays elevated for nearly two weeks. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estradiol stimulating proliferation of the endometrial lining

choices.label: B
choices.text: GnRH pulses accelerating from hypothalamic inputs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibin acting on the anterior pituitary to decrease FSH

choices.label: D
choices.text: LH acting on theca cells to increase androgen synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Progesterone acting on the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center

explanation.summary: Luteal-phase progesterone raises body temperature by affecting the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center.
explanation.whyCorrect: After ovulation, luteal cells of the corpus luteum synthesize large amounts of progesterone. Among its functions, progesterone increases body temperature by acting on the thermoregulatory center of the hypothalamus, which explains the sustained post-ovulatory temperature rise.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estradiol's proliferative effect on the endometrium occurs before ovulation and does not raise body temperature.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GnRH pulse frequency governs gonadotropin release, not the post-ovulatory temperature elevation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin regulates FSH secretion and has no described thermoregulatory role.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LH-driven theca-cell androgen synthesis feeds estrogen production; it does not change the temperature set point.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old competitive weightlifter comes to the clinic because he and his partner have been unable to conceive for 14 months. For the past 2 years he has self-administered injectable anabolic-androgenic steroids obtained at his gym. Examination shows well-developed musculature, blood pressure of 144/92 mm Hg, and small, soft testes bilaterally. Semen analysis shows a markedly decreased sperm count. Which of the following best explains his impaired spermatogenesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acquired loss of androgen-receptor function in Sertoli cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoimmune disruption of the blood-testis barrier and germ cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated inhibin B secretion with selective suppression of LH

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased 5-alpha-reductase activity within the seminiferous tubules

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppressed gonadotropin secretion with low intratesticular testosterone

explanation.summary: Exogenous androgens suppress the HPG axis, lowering intratesticular testosterone and Sertoli-cell stimulation despite high circulating androgen levels.
explanation.whyCorrect: Exogenous androgens provide negative feedback to the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary, decreasing GnRH, LH, and FSH secretion. Reduced LH lowers Leydig-cell output, so intratesticular testosterone falls, and reduced FSH withdraws Sertoli-cell stimulation. Spermatogenesis requires FSH plus a high local testosterone concentration, so sperm production declines and the testes atrophy even though circulating androgen levels are high.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Androgen receptors are intact; the problem is loss of gonadotropin drive and local testosterone, not receptor failure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nothing in the history suggests autoimmune testicular injury; the findings are explained by hormonal suppression from the injected steroids.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin B is secreted by Sertoli cells and selectively inhibits FSH, not LH; with Sertoli-cell suppression, inhibin B would fall rather than rise.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Conversion of testosterone to DHT by 5-alpha-reductase is a normal target-tissue event and does not impair spermatogenesis.

questions.stem: During male fetal development, differentiation of the penis, scrotum, and prostate is primarily induced by which of the following hormones?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Androstenedione

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dehydroepiandrosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dihydrotestosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone

explanation.summary: DHT masculinizes the external genitalia and prostate, while testosterone masculinizes the Wolffian-duct derivatives.
explanation.whyCorrect: DHT, formed from testosterone by 5-alpha-reductase in target tissues, induces differentiation of the penis, scrotum, prostate, and male urethra during fetal development. It is a more potent androgen-receptor agonist than testosterone and acts largely within the tissues where it is produced.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Androstenedione is a weak precursor androgen that must be converted to testosterone or estrogens to exert significant effects.
whyWrongByChoice.B: DHEA is a weak adrenal androgen contributing to pubic and axillary hair, body odor, and sebaceous activity, mainly after peripheral conversion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Estradiol, formed by aromatization of testosterone, promotes epiphyseal plate maturation and closure rather than masculinizing external genitalia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Testosterone directly induces the Wolffian-duct derivatives (epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal vesicles), not the external genitalia and prostate.

questions.stem: A study of male reproductive development examines the hormonal requirements for differentiation of the epididymis, ductus deferens, and seminal vesicles from the Wolffian ducts. Differentiation of these structures depends most directly on which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DHEAS secreted by the fetal adrenal gland

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dihydrotestosterone formed in genital skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estradiol formed by aromatization in peripheral tissues

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibin B secreted by fetal Sertoli cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone secreted by fetal Leydig cells

explanation.summary: Testosterone from fetal Leydig cells drives Wolffian-duct differentiation into the epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal vesicles, and ejaculatory ducts.
explanation.whyCorrect: During fetal development, testicular testosterone production supports differentiation of the Wolffian-duct structures, including the epididymides, vasa deferentia, seminal vesicles, and ejaculatory ducts. This is a direct action of testosterone, distinct from the DHT-dependent masculinization of the external genitalia and prostate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adrenal DHEAS is a weak androgen precursor whose main contributions are pubic and axillary hair, body odor, and sebaceous activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: DHT mediates differentiation of the penis, scrotum, prostate, and male urethra, not the Wolffian-duct derivatives.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estradiol from aromatization of testosterone contributes to epiphyseal maturation and negative feedback, not Wolffian-duct differentiation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin B regulates pituitary FSH secretion; it does not induce differentiation of Wolffian-duct structures.

questions.stem: In a physiology experiment, a healthy 25-year-old man receives a continuous infusion of inhibin B at a concentration sufficient to act on the pituitary. Which of the following changes in his hormone levels is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased FSH with a marked fall in circulating testosterone and LH

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased FSH with LH and testosterone relatively unchanged

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreased hypothalamic GnRH pulses with loss of both gonadotropins

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decreased LH with FSH and testosterone relatively unchanged

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased FSH and increased LH with a rise in testosterone

explanation.summary: Inhibin B acts primarily on the anterior pituitary to selectively decrease FSH secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inhibin B, normally secreted by Sertoli cells, selectively inhibits FSH secretion at the anterior pituitary. Because the LH-Leydig-cell branch is regulated chiefly by sex-steroid feedback rather than by inhibin, LH and testosterone remain relatively unchanged while FSH falls.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Testosterone production is driven by LH, which inhibin B does not suppress, so a marked fall in testosterone is not expected.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin B acts primarily at the anterior pituitary on FSH; it is not described as shutting down hypothalamic GnRH pulses or both gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin B does not selectively suppress LH; LH secretion is governed mainly by testosterone and estradiol feedback.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibin B is inhibitory to the pituitary; it does not raise gonadotropin secretion.

questions.stem: During the first half of gestation, Leydig cells in a male fetus actively secrete testosterone, supporting differentiation of the internal genital ducts before the fetal hypothalamic-pituitary axis is fully mature. At this stage, Leydig-cell testosterone synthesis is stimulated primarily by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ACTH from the fetal anterior pituitary

choices.label: B
choices.text: FSH from the fetal anterior pituitary

choices.label: C
choices.text: GnRH acting directly on the testis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: E
choices.text: LH from the fetal anterior pituitary

explanation.summary: Fetal Leydig cells synthesize testosterone in response to hCG; LH takes over this role after puberty.
explanation.whyCorrect: Leydig cells respond to hCG during fetal development and to LH after puberty. hCG activates LH receptors on Leydig cells, driving the testosterone production that supports fetal Wolffian-duct differentiation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ACTH regulates adrenal-cortex steroid output, including adrenal androgens at adrenarche, not testicular testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: FSH acts on Sertoli cells within the seminiferous tubules, not on Leydig-cell testosterone synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GnRH acts on gonadotropes in the anterior pituitary via the portal circulation; it does not directly stimulate the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: LH becomes the principal Leydig-cell stimulus after puberty; during fetal development the stimulus is hCG.

questions.stem: A researcher measuring sex-steroid levels in healthy adult men notes that testosterone, like other steroid hormones, has a lipid-soluble four-ring structure that does not dissolve freely in plasma. In the bloodstream, most circulating testosterone is transported in which of the following ways?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bound to circulating inhibin B secreted by Sertoli cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bound to sex hormone-binding globulin or albumin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Carried within the cytoplasm of circulating erythrocytes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Covalently attached to circulating androgen receptors

choices.label: E
choices.text: Freely dissolved in the aqueous plasma as unbound hormone

explanation.summary: Most circulating testosterone travels bound to sex hormone-binding globulin or albumin; only a small unbound fraction is available to tissues.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because their fused steroid rings make them lipophilic, androgens cannot dissolve freely in plasma. Binding to sex hormone-binding globulin or albumin permits transport in the aqueous bloodstream and regulates the small unbound fraction that can diffuse into target cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhibin B is a Sertoli-cell hormone that regulates FSH; it is not a plasma carrier for testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Testosterone is carried by plasma binding proteins, not inside red blood cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Androgen receptors are intracellular; testosterone binds them noncovalently after entering the target cell, not during transport.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Only a small fraction of testosterone circulates unbound; its lipophilicity prevents most of it from dissolving freely in plasma.

questions.stem: In a prostate epithelial cell, testosterone diffuses across the plasma membrane and is converted by 5-alpha-reductase to DHT, which binds an intracellular androgen receptor. Which of the following events occurs next in this signaling pathway?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The androgen-bound receptor opens a ligand-gated cation channel in the plasma membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: The receptor activates a membrane-bound G protein that raises cyclic AMP

choices.label: C
choices.text: The receptor complex blocks translation of target mRNAs at the ribosome

choices.label: D
choices.text: The receptor complex dimerizes, enters the nucleus, and binds androgen-response elements

choices.label: E
choices.text: The receptor phosphorylates tyrosine residues on cytosolic substrate proteins

explanation.summary: Activated androgen receptors translocate to the nucleus, dimerize, bind androgen-response elements, and regulate gene transcription.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testosterone or DHT binds an intracellular androgen receptor; the activated receptor translocates to the nucleus, forms dimers, binds androgen-response elements in DNA, and regulates transcription of target genes into mRNA that is then translated into protein. In the prostate, DHT is the predominant androgen-receptor ligand.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Androgens act through intracellular receptors that alter transcription, not through ligand-gated ion channels.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Androgen receptors are nuclear transcription regulators, not G protein-coupled receptors that signal through cyclic AMP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The activated receptor regulates transcription of target genes; it does not act by blocking translation at the ribosome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The androgen receptor is not a tyrosine kinase; its action is to regulate gene transcription.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old patient with a 46,XY karyotype is evaluated for absent pubertal virilization. Examination shows female-pattern external genitalia, and imaging reveals intra-abdominal testes. Circulating testosterone is within the adult male reference range, and a trial of androgen therapy produces no virilization. Which of the following best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absent Leydig-cell testosterone synthesis during fetal development

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deficient 5-alpha-reductase activity in genital skin and urogenital sinus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excess aromatization of androgens to estradiol in peripheral tissues

choices.label: D
choices.text: Failure of placental hCG stimulation of fetal Leydig cells in utero

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nonfunctional intracellular androgen receptors in target tissues

explanation.summary: In complete androgen insensitivity syndrome, a 46,XY individual with testes has nonfunctional androgen receptors, so androgen-dependent masculinization cannot occur.
explanation.whyCorrect: Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome results from nonfunctional androgen receptors in a 46,XY individual with testes. Androgens are produced but cannot act, so external genital development follows a typically female pattern. Because the receptor itself is defective, giving more androgen is ineffective, which explains the failed therapeutic trial.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Circulating testosterone is in the adult male range, so Leydig-cell synthesis is clearly preserved.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A 5-alpha-reductase problem would leave receptor-mediated testosterone actions intact, so a trial of androgen therapy would not be entirely without effect; the complete unresponsiveness points to the receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The findings reflect absent androgen action rather than excess estrogen production; the key clue is that androgen treatment is ineffective.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Testes formed and produce testosterone, so fetal Leydig-cell stimulation was adequate; the defect is downstream at the receptor.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with a 20-year history of heavy daily alcohol use reports decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. Examination shows bilateral, tender enlargement of glandular breast tissue. Along with suppression of GnRH and LH secretion, which of the following mechanisms best explains his breast findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enhanced 5-alpha-reduction of testosterone in breast tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess inhibin B secretion from Sertoli cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Impaired hepatic metabolism and clearance of estrogens

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased Leydig-cell testosterone production

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased pulsatile GnRH secretion from the hypothalamus

explanation.summary: Chronic alcohol use suppresses the HPG axis and, through liver dysfunction, impairs estrogen clearance, producing increased estrogenic effects such as gynecomastia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic alcohol use lowers testosterone by decreasing hypothalamic GnRH release, directly inhibiting pituitary LH secretion, and impairing Leydig- and Sertoli-cell function. Alcohol-associated liver dysfunction additionally impairs hepatic estrogen metabolism and clearance, so estrogenic effects increase, which can produce loss of libido, sexual dysfunction, and gynecomastia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DHT formation drives androgenic effects such as prostate growth and balding; gynecomastia here reflects excess estrogenic effect from poor hepatic clearance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic alcohol use impairs Sertoli-cell function; rising inhibin B is not the mechanism, and inhibin B acts on FSH rather than causing breast growth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Alcohol reduces Leydig-cell stimulation and testosterone production; increased testosterone output would not explain this picture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Alcohol decreases GnRH release from the hypothalamus; it does not increase it.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old girl is brought to the clinic because of new body odor and a small amount of pubic hair. She has no breast development, and her growth curve is unchanged. Increased secretion of which of the following best accounts for these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DHEA and DHEAS from the adrenal cortex

choices.label: B
choices.text: DHT produced within genital skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estradiol from the ovaries

choices.label: D
choices.text: LH and FSH from the anterior pituitary

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone from ovarian theca cells

explanation.summary: Adrenarche, driven by ACTH-regulated adrenal androgen output, precedes gonadal puberty and produces pubic and axillary hair, body odor, and sebaceous activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: During adrenarche, the adrenal cortex becomes the principal source of rising circulating androgens under ACTH regulation, before gonadal puberty begins. Adrenal androgens such as DHEA and DHEAS contribute to pubic and axillary hair growth, body odor, and sebaceous-gland activity, partly through peripheral conversion to more potent androgens.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Local DHT formation is downstream of available androgen precursors; the primary change at adrenarche is increased adrenal DHEA and DHEAS output.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rising estradiol would produce breast development, which is absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gonadotropin activation marks gonadal puberty; adrenarche occurs before it and is ACTH-regulated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ovarian theca-cell androgen production is stimulated by LH with gonadal puberty; the absence of breast development indicates the gonadal axis has not yet activated.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy completing puberty is noted to have progressive slowing of linear growth as his skeletal maturation advances. The maturation and closure of his epiphyseal growth plates is promoted primarily by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DHEAS secreted by the adrenal cortex

choices.label: B
choices.text: DHT formed by 5-alpha-reduction of testosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estradiol formed by aromatization of testosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibin B secreted by Sertoli cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone acting directly on androgen receptors in bone

explanation.summary: Aromatization of testosterone to estradiol promotes epiphyseal plate maturation and closure at the end of puberty.
explanation.whyCorrect: While testosterone contributes to voice deepening, libido, muscle growth, and spermatogenesis, its conversion by aromatase to estradiol is what promotes epiphyseal plate maturation and closure, ending linear growth as puberty completes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adrenal DHEAS is a weak androgen precursor contributing to hair, odor, and sebaceous activity, not epiphyseal closure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: DHT mediates prostate growth, male-pattern balding, and sebaceous activity, not epiphyseal closure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin B regulates pituitary FSH secretion and has no described role in growth-plate closure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Epiphyseal maturation is attributed to estradiol produced from testosterone, not to direct androgen-receptor action of testosterone.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old male cyclist is found on routine laboratory testing to have a hemoglobin of 18.6 g/dL and a hematocrit of 56%. He is well hydrated, has no lung disease, and lives at sea level. He reports 8 months of daily use of an unprescribed powder containing "male hormones" that his trainer supplied. Which of the following best explains his laboratory findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A primary clonal myeloproliferative disorder

choices.label: B
choices.text: Androgen-stimulated increase in red-blood-cell production

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chronic arterial hypoxemia stimulating erythropoiesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Erythropoietin secretion from a renal tumor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hemoconcentration from reduced plasma volume

explanation.summary: Supraphysiologic androgen exposure increases red-blood-cell production and can cause erythrocytosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Androgens support erythropoiesis during adulthood, and although erythropoietin is the principal hormonal regulator of red-cell production, supraphysiologic androgen exposure can increase red-blood-cell production and cause erythrocytosis. In a patient taking an unprescribed androgen-containing supplement, the elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit are best explained by this androgen effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A clonal marrow disorder is not suggested when a known erythrocytosis-producing exposure, supraphysiologic androgens, accounts for the findings.
whyWrongByChoice.C: He has no lung disease and lives at sea level, so chronic hypoxemia is not a plausible driver of his erythrocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no evidence of a renal mass; the temporal link to androgen use points to the supplement as the cause.
whyWrongByChoice.E: He is well hydrated, so a spurious rise in hematocrit from reduced plasma volume is unlikely.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman with regular 28-day cycles is on day 8 of her cycle. Serum estradiol is rising as a cohort of antral follicles grows. FSH most directly increases estradiol production during this phase by stimulating which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Androstenedione synthesis by theca cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aromatase activity in granulosa cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: GnRH pulse frequency in the hypothalamus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Progesterone secretion by the corpus luteum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vascularization of the outer theca layer

explanation.summary: FSH stimulates granulosa-cell aromatase to convert theca-derived androstenedione to estradiol.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the two-cell mechanism, LH stimulates theca cells to produce androstenedione, which diffuses to granulosa cells. FSH then stimulates granulosa-cell aromatase to convert that androstenedione to estradiol, driving the follicular-phase estradiol rise.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Androstenedione production by theca cells is stimulated by LH, not FSH.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GnRH originates in the hypothalamus and drives pituitary FSH release, not the reverse.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The corpus luteum does not exist during the follicular phase; it forms only after ovulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Theca vascularization is a structural feature of secondary-follicle development, not the direct FSH-dependent step in estradiol synthesis.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman is on day 13 of a 28-day cycle. Serum studies show estradiol that has remained markedly elevated for the past two days, produced by a single dominant follicle. Which of the following hormonal events is most likely to occur next?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A rise in FSH driven by increased inhibin B

choices.label: B
choices.text: A rise in trophoblast-derived hCG secretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: A sharp increase in progesterone from theca cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: A surge in LH secretion from the anterior pituitary

choices.label: E
choices.text: A sustained fall in GnRH pulse activity

explanation.summary: Sustained high estradiol late in the follicular phase switches to positive feedback and generates the preovulatory LH surge.
explanation.whyCorrect: During most of the follicular phase estradiol suppresses gonadotropin secretion, but sustained high estradiol late in the follicular phase produces positive feedback on the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary. This generates the LH surge that triggers ovulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhibin B decreases FSH secretion rather than raising it; FSH is falling at this point in the cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: hCG is produced by trophoblast cells only after implantation, not at midcycle in a nonpregnant woman.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Progesterone rises after ovulation from the corpus luteum; theca cells produce androstenedione during the follicular phase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sustained high estradiol produces positive feedback at the hypothalamus and pituitary, not suppression of GnRH activity.

questions.stem: During an in vitro fertilization procedure, an oocyte is retrieved shortly after its release from a dominant follicle. Before any contact with sperm, this oocyte is in which stage of meiosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Actively undergoing cleavage divisions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arrested in metaphase of meiosis I

choices.label: C
choices.text: Arrested in metaphase of meiosis II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Arrested in prophase of meiosis I

choices.label: E
choices.text: Completed meiosis II with a mature ovum

explanation.summary: Ovulation releases a secondary oocyte arrested in metaphase II, which completes meiosis II only if fertilization occurs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ovulation is the release of a secondary oocyte arrested in metaphase II from the dominant follicle. Meiosis II is completed only if fertilization occurs, after which the zygote undergoes cleavage and develops into a blastocyst.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cleavage occurs in the zygote after fertilization, not in an unfertilized oocyte.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The LH surge causes the primary oocyte to complete meiosis I before ovulation; the released cell has passed this stage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prophase I arrest describes the primary oocyte within primordial follicles, before the LH surge causes completion of meiosis I.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Meiosis II is completed only after fertilization, which has not occurred in this oocyte.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman with regular 28-day cycles develops sudden right lower-quadrant pain on day 14 of her cycle. The pain is unilateral, moderate, and resolves over the next day without intervention. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her pain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Atresia of the nondominant follicles in the recruited cohort

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breakdown and shedding of the functional endometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Follicular rupture with limited bleeding irritating the peritoneum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regression of the corpus luteum into a corpus albicans

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trophoblast invasion of the secretory endometrium

explanation.summary: Mittelschmerz is unilateral lower-abdominal pain from peritoneal irritation caused by follicular rupture and limited bleeding at ovulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Midcycle unilateral lower-abdominal pain in a woman with regular cycles is characteristic of mittelschmerz. It results from peritoneal irritation associated with follicular rupture and limited bleeding during ovulation, which occurs near day 14 of a 28-day cycle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atresia of nondominant follicles occurs as FSH declines during the follicular phase and is not described as a cause of peritoneal pain.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endometrial shedding causes menstruation beginning on day 1 of the cycle, not midcycle unilateral pain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Corpus luteum regression occurs late in the luteal phase and precedes menstruation; it does not cause midcycle pain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trophoblast invasion accompanies implantation after fertilization and is not a midcycle event in this patient.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman conceives during the current cycle. Three weeks after ovulation, her serum progesterone remains elevated and no menstruation has occurred. Which of the following best explains the continued progesterone secretion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhibin A stimulates luteal progesterone synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: LH from the anterior pituitary continues to rise after implantation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sustained estradiol exerts positive feedback on the corpus luteum

choices.label: D
choices.text: The corpus albicans takes over steroid secretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trophoblast-derived hCG maintains the corpus luteum

explanation.summary: After implantation, trophoblast-derived hCG maintains the corpus luteum and its progesterone secretion during early pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: In a nonpregnant luteal phase, absence of hCG allows the corpus luteum to regress, ovarian steroids to fall, and menstruation to follow. When implantation occurs, trophoblast cells produce hCG, which maintains the corpus luteum and its progesterone secretion until placental steroid production becomes sufficient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhibin A suppresses FSH secretion; it is a product of the corpus luteum, not a stimulus for progesterone synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Luteal progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A suppress gonadotropin secretion; pituitary LH does not rise to rescue the corpus luteum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estradiol's positive feedback acts on the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary to generate the LH surge, not on the corpus luteum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The corpus albicans is the fibrotic remnant that forms after the corpus luteum's endocrine function ends; it does not secrete steroids.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman is on day 2 of her menstrual cycle. Compared with the late luteal phase of her previous cycle, her serum FSH concentration has risen. Which of the following best explains this rise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased negative feedback after regression of the corpus luteum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased inhibin B secretion from the newly recruited follicular cohort

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased LH-receptor expression on dominant follicle granulosa cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Positive feedback from sustained high estradiol concentrations

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rising hCG secretion from the newly shed endometrial lining

explanation.summary: Corpus luteum regression removes progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A negative feedback, allowing FSH to rise at the start of the follicular phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Regression of the previous cycle's corpus luteum decreases progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A. The resulting reduction in negative feedback on the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary allows FSH to rise, supporting growth of a new cohort of gonadotropin-responsive follicles.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Inhibin B from developing follicles decreases FSH secretion; it does not cause FSH to rise.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FSH promotes LH-receptor expression in the dominant follicle during late follicular maturation; this is a downstream event, not the cause of the early FSH rise.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sustained high estradiol occurs late in the follicular phase and generates the LH surge, not the early-cycle FSH rise.
whyWrongByChoice.E: hCG is produced by trophoblast cells only when implantation occurs, and menstruation indicates implantation did not occur.

questions.stem: During the mid-follicular phase, rising estradiol and inhibin B cause serum FSH to decline, yet a single follicle continues maturing toward ovulation while the rest of the recruited cohort degenerates. Which of the following properties best explains why this follicle survives?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It contains an oocyte that has already completed meiosis I

choices.label: B
choices.text: It develops a vascularized granulosa-cell compartment

choices.label: C
choices.text: It escapes gonadotropin dependence at the antral stage

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the most responsive to FSH of all the growing follicles

choices.label: E
choices.text: It secretes inhibin A that stimulates its own granulosa cells

explanation.summary: As FSH declines under estradiol and inhibin B feedback, the follicle most responsive to FSH becomes dominant while less-responsive follicles undergo atresia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estradiol and inhibin B decrease FSH secretion during the follicular phase. As FSH declines, less-responsive follicles undergo atresia, while the follicle most responsive to FSH continues maturing as the dominant follicle; FSH also promotes LH-receptor expression in its granulosa cells during late maturation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The primary oocyte completes meiosis I only in response to the LH surge, just before ovulation, not at selection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The granulosa-cell compartment remains avascular; it is the theca that becomes vascularized.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antral follicles are gonadotropin dependent; dominance reflects superior FSH responsiveness, not independence from gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibin A from the dominant follicle contributes to FSH suppression at the pituitary; it is not described as a self-stimulating growth signal.

questions.stem: A reproductive physiologist studies a granulosa-cell hormone that rises as a cohort of follicles develops during the follicular phase and selectively decreases pituitary secretion of FSH without an equivalent effect on LH. Which of the following hormones is being studied?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibin A

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibin B

choices.label: E
choices.text: Progesterone

explanation.summary: Inhibin B from granulosa cells of developing follicles selectively decreases FSH secretion during the follicular phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inhibin B is produced by granulosa cells of developing follicles during the follicular phase and selectively decreases FSH secretion. This selective FSH suppression contributes to atresia of less-responsive follicles and selection of the dominant follicle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estradiol suppresses gonadotropin secretion broadly during most of the follicular phase rather than selectively targeting FSH.
whyWrongByChoice.B: hCG is produced by trophoblast cells after implantation and maintains the corpus luteum; it is not a granulosa-cell feedback hormone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibin A is produced by the dominant follicle late in the follicular phase and predominantly by the corpus luteum during the luteal phase, not by the developing cohort early on.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progesterone is a corpus luteum product of the luteal phase, not a granulosa-cell hormone of the developing cohort.

questions.stem: An endometrial biopsy obtained from a healthy 27-year-old woman on day 10 of her cycle shows regenerating glands and stroma of the functional layer with abundant mitotic figures. Which of the following hormones is primarily responsible for these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Follicle-stimulating hormone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Progesterone

explanation.summary: Estradiol from developing follicles drives regeneration and proliferation of the functional endometrium during the proliferative phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Day 10 falls in the proliferative phase, which runs from the end of menstruation to ovulation. Estradiol produced by developing follicles stimulates regeneration and proliferation of the glandular epithelium and stroma of the functional endometrium and induces progesterone-receptor expression.

whyWrongByChoice.B: FSH acts on granulosa cells to support follicular maturation and estradiol synthesis; it is not the direct endometrial stimulus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG maintains the corpus luteum after implantation and has no role in a day-10 proliferative endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LH acts on theca cells and triggers ovulation; it does not directly stimulate endometrial proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progesterone acts after ovulation, decreasing mitotic activity and producing secretory change; it does not drive proliferation.

questions.stem: An endometrial biopsy from a healthy 33-year-old woman on day 22 of a 28-day cycle shows tortuous, actively secreting glands, stromal maturation, and markedly decreased mitotic activity. These changes are primarily produced by a hormone secreted from which of the following sources?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gonadotropes of the anterior pituitary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Granulosa cells of the dominant follicle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lipid-rich cells of the corpus luteum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Theca cells of recruited antral follicles

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trophoblast cells of an implanting blastocyst

explanation.summary: Progesterone from the corpus luteum transforms the estradiol-primed endometrium into secretory tissue during the secretory phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Day 22 is in the secretory phase. Progesterone from the corpus luteum, a highly vascular temporary endocrine structure whose lipid-rich cells synthesize progesterone and estradiol, decreases mitotic activity and produces tortuous secretory glands and stromal changes that make the endometrium receptive to implantation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anterior-pituitary gonadotropes secrete LH and FSH, which act on the ovary, not directly on the endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulosa cells of the dominant follicle produce estradiol during the follicular phase, which drives proliferation rather than secretory change.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Theca cells produce androstenedione as an estradiol precursor; they are not the source of the secretory-phase hormone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trophoblast cells secrete hCG after implantation; secretory transformation occurs whether or not implantation happens.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman requests combined oral contraceptive pills and asks how they prevent pregnancy so effectively. Which of the following best describes their primary mechanism of action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accelerating atresia of the primordial follicle pool in both ovaries

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blocking completion of meiosis II after the oocyte is fertilized

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inducing early regression of the corpus luteum after ovulation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stimulating proliferation of the functional endometrial layer

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppressing gonadotropin secretion, preventing the LH surge and ovulation

explanation.summary: Combined oral contraceptives suppress gonadotropin secretion through negative feedback, preventing the LH surge required for ovulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Combined oral contraceptives act primarily through negative feedback that suppresses gonadotropin secretion, so the LH surge required for ovulation never occurs. The progestin component additionally thickens cervical mucus and reduces endometrial receptivity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The finite follicle pool declines through atresia across the lifespan regardless of contraception; pills do not act by destroying the ovarian reserve.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Preventing pregnancy by these pills occurs upstream, at ovulation; they do not act by arresting meiosis after fertilization.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Their mechanism prevents ovulation from happening, rather than causing luteal regression after an ovulation has occurred.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progestins reduce endometrial receptivity; stimulating endometrial proliferation is an estradiol effect of the normal cycle, not a contraceptive mechanism.
